title: National Standard for Driver & Rider Training
whatItIs: DVSA's standard setting out the skills, knowledge and understanding needed to deliver driver and rider training. Part 3 and the standards check are assessed against it.
keyFacts: It assumes trainers have mastered roles 1 to 4 of the driving standard and shown competence in role 5.
Candidates are expected to show at least level 3 competence.
Unit 1: confirm you're legal to train; display or carry your certificate as the law requires.
Unit 5: evaluate and develop yourself, e.g. keep a reflective log and know the standards check.
In the standard, 'learner' can mean a novice, partly trained, trained or experienced driver or rider.

a.label: Driving standard (car, cat B)
points: What a safe, responsible driver must do and know
5 roles, from preparing to lifelong review

b.label: Driver and rider training standard
points: What an instructor must do and know to train
6 units, from legal checks to role play

onTheTest.question: Which element of the National standard for driver and rider training is about coaching?
onTheTest.why: Unit 3 has 4 elements: 6.3.1 Create a climate that promotes learning, 6.3.2 Explain and demonstrate, 6.3.3 Coach, 6.3.4 Facilitate group-based learning.

onTheTest.question: Which unit of the training standard covers managing the risk of violence in the learning environment?
onTheTest.why: Unit 4 Manage risk to instructor, learner and third parties: 6.4.1 on-road risk, 6.4.2 risk of violence, 6.4.3 health and safety in the classroom.

traps: The first 3 elements of unit 3 are layers of one approach: client-centred learning.
Role play: simulate high-risk faults verbally where possible; no faults involving vulnerable road users.
Not all instructors choose classroom delivery, but it's a core skill for motorcycle instructors.
